scope: loopback QoS0 PUBLISH echo through Goose stream adapter and Python TCP bridge
limitations: Only MQTT 3.1.1 CONNECT, SUBSCRIBE, QoS0 PUBLISH echo, DISCONNECT path exercised.
Payload sizes are small and bounded by RX=TX=256; no claim for larger frames or other QoS.
Loopback WSL measurements include Python IPC, socket calls, broker work and Goose codec/adapter work.
No comparison or speedup claim; results describe this machine and exact harness only.
RSS uses 1 ms /proc VmRSS polling for bridge, Goose child and broker; combined is sampled concurrent sum, excludes runner and setup/install.

configuration.allowed_limits: payload sizes fixed at 16 and 192 bytes; --samples 7..20; --iterations 1..1000; --warmup 0..50; each batch has a 60 s bridge watchdog and 90 s outer subprocess timeout
configuration.timing: Goose clock_ns() immediately before payload generation/encoding and after complete echoed PUBLISH parse, sequence/topic/payload validation, and stream commit; start/end ticks are buffered then emitted after the measured loop so no event IPC lies inside an echo; throughput is first start to final end
configuration.setup_excluded: native compile, npm install, broker start, TCP connect, MQTT CONNECT/SUBSCRIBE and per-connection warmup
configuration.payload: first four bytes are a big-endian per-exchange sequence; remaining bytes are deterministic from position and sequence; every echoed byte and topic checked in Goose before completion event, preventing an earlier echo from satisfying a later operation
configuration.memory: 1ms nominal /proc VmRSS sampling during each batch; bridge, Goose child and broker component maxima are separate; combined_sampled_sum_max_kib is the maximum sum of page counts read sequentially in one nominal sampling round, may include shared pages and miss transients, and is not a strict instantaneous or unique-memory peak; excludes compile/setup/install and runner
